review_notes: I read the whole file. I searched Mathlib for competing versions of the main declarations: `extendRingHom`, `extensionHom`, `mapRingHom`, `sepQuotHomeomorphRingQuot`, `sepQuotRingEquivRingQuot` and `inseparableSetoid_ring`. The only other uses of `IsDenseInducing.extendRingHom` are in `Topology/Instances/Complex.lean` and `RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Evaluation.lean`. Both call the file's own definition, so they are not independent duplicates. I found no other ring-level extension of dense inducing maps and no other identification of `SeparationQuotient` with the quotient by `Ideal.closure ⊥`. `mapRingHom` is a named ring-homomorphism wrapper over `Completion.map`, and it is related to it by `rfl` lemmas. The task allows such named wrappers. `extensionHom` and `extendRingHom` are different constructions, built on `Completion.extension` and on the generic dense-inducing `extend` respectively. I found no case for consolidating any of them. I did not look for a continuous-ring-hom bundled type that `extensionHom` could take in place of its separate `hf : Continuous f` argument, so a small uncertainty remains there.
